Jack Heart explicitly accepts best-effort shutdown: "best effort shut down is ok but do we not have guardian processes?" He also asks whether RunPod is best-effort or guaranteed. Investigation confirms existing Etude RunPod/Vast shutdown is best-effort: standard-library guardian starts before dependency installs, uses self-scoped provider credentials, and requests deletion at the time/cost deadline; it cannot run during preboot/image pull and provider/network failures can delay deletion. docs/launcher.md already documents these gaps. The original task brief overstated guarantees; do not impose stronger absolute guarantees on Lium or continue blocking implementation on undocumented deletion slack. Proceed with supported layered protection: termination_hours in initial creation, exact scheduled deletion immediately after receipt with acknowledgement/readback, controller cleanup/reconciliation/retries, and local job deadline/watchdog before dependency installation where feasible. Reuse the shared guardian/bootstrap machinery where compatible. Distinguish killing work from ending provider billing. Determine whether Lium supplies a pod-scoped self-deletion credential; never copy the broad account API key onto a rented worker merely to reuse the guardian. If no safe machine-scoped deletion authority exists, use provider timer plus controller removal and state the difference plainly. Per-key spending caps are an additional optional operator backstop, not a newly required prerequisite to implementation/publication and not permission to change account settings. Preserve planned allocation limits, conservative quote/reservation and actual-cost accounting; user did not raise the USD10 TLA budget or authorize intentionally overspending. Best-effort timing/cleanup is accepted, not a guarantee of zero overrun. Update the brief/design/docs, implement and test the lifecycle, and continue the existing authorized auto delivery. Lium only; no TensorDock. This accepted safeguard revision resolves the repeated blocker and is a reason to resume.
